name: auditLogs__publicList
description:
Returns a paginated list of audit log entries scoped to the authenticated principal.

Workspace-scoped sessions and API tokens see only their workspace; org admins and API tokens scoped to `all_workspaces_in_org` see every workspace in their organization.

Sorted by `timestamp` descending. Use the returned `next_cursor` (when present) as the `cursor` query parameter on the next request to continue paging.

name: attackPaths__list
description:
Retrieves all attack paths discovered within a workspace. Attack path is a condition in which an asset is both externally exploitable and has a cloud blast radius that allows it to potentially interact with or compromise internal resources.

Each response entry includes the attack path ID, severity, associated finding types, and violations count.

Use this endpoint to review all known attack paths, track exposed resources, and prioritize remediation efforts across the environment.

name: attackPaths__violations
description:
Retrieves all resources that are violating security posture rules and, as a result, create an attack path condition.

An attack path occurs when an asset is both externally exploitable and has a cloud blast radius that allows it to potentially interact with or compromise internal resources.

The response includes the resource IDs along with the timestamps indicating when each resource began violating the rule.

name: attackPaths__details
description:
Retrieves the complete attack path for a specified resource, showing the sequence of network and security components an attacker could traverse to reach it.

The response returns one or more ordered paths, starting from the origin (e.g., Internet) and listing each intermediate element such as gateways, ACLs, security groups, load balancers, or other relevant resources.

Parameters include the unique resource_id (required) and the optional workspace context.

Use this endpoint to visualize potential exposure, assess lateral movement risk, and prioritize remediation actions.

name: canaries__list
description:
Retrieves a list of all deployed and configured canary resources across monitored accounts.

A canary resource is a controlled, decoy asset - such as an S3 bucket - used to detect unauthorized activity by triggering alerts when predefined detection actions occur.

This endpoint supports filtering by account ID, region, resource type, status, creator, and other attributes. Optional parameters allow inclusion of related activity logs for each canary.

Returned objects include canary metadata, deployment status, detection settings, exclusion rules, and recent activity indicators.

name: configChanges__list
description:
Retrieves recent configuration changes -write audit events analyzed for security impact, such as internet exposure, privilege escalation, or new database access.

The response includes what was changed, its severity and time, affected resources, related user and network details, along with any linked events and raw data.

Use this endpoint to investigate recent changes to understand their security implications and identify potential risks.

pageIndex.description: The 0-based index of the page to retrieve.

pageSize.description: The number of items to retrieve per page.

name: configChanges__details
description:
Retrieves the full details of a specific configuration change by its unique ID, including associated violations and attack paths.

Configuration changes are write audit events analyzed for security impact, such as internet exposure, privilege escalation, or new database access.

Use this endpoint to investigate the change, assess its risk, and understand potential exploitation paths.

name: inventory__list
description:
Retrieves cloud and platform resources across monitored environments, returning normalized metadata such as resource ID, type, display name, account ID, region, cloud provider, parent lineage, public accessibility status, and end timestamp.

This endpoint is useful for building an inventory, performing lookups, and pivoting between related assets.

IMPORTANT: `resource_type` accepts only canonical short names (e.g. "eks", "instance", "bucket", "network_acl"). When you have a guess from a runbook description (e.g. "EKS cluster" → eks_cluster, "EC2 instance" → ec2_instance), call inventory__resolveResourceType FIRST to map it to the canonical name. This saves a wasted call against the typesMap validator.

phrase.description: Search resources by IDs, IPs or display names

tags.description: List of Key:Value pairs delimited by ":"

name: inventory__details
description:
Retrieves detailed metadata and configuration for a specific resource, including its type, display name, cloud provider, account, region, accessibility status, tags, and associated network interfaces.

The response also includes translated and enriched data such as cluster or namespace context, container specifications, environment variables, volume mounts, owner references, conditions, and node selectors. Depending on the resource type, additional attributes like security settings, probes, and connected services may be included.

Use this endpoint to obtain a comprehensive view of a resource’s identity, configuration, and operational state for inventory, compliance, or investigation purposes.

IMPORTANT: Use the full resource ARN or resource_id from inventory__list results.

name: inventory__configuration
description:
Retrieves the translated configuration data for a specific resource by its ID.

The translated data contains enriched and normalized resource attributes, which vary depending on the resource type and cloud provider. This may include identity details, networking, tags, hierarchical context, and provider-specific settings.

Use this endpoint to obtain a resource’s processed configuration for inventory browsing, compliance review, or investigation purposes.

IMPORTANT: Use the full resource ARN or resource_id from inventory__list results.

name: inventory__rawConfiguration
description:
Retrieves the raw, unprocessed provider configuration for a specific resource by its ID.

This is the verbatim payload as returned by the cloud provider and is larger than the translated view. Use /inventory/resource/configuration for enriched, normalized attributes.

name: inventory__type
description:
Returns a summary of resources grouped by type, including the count of each resource type across the environment.

Use this endpoint to quickly assess resource distribution and identify concentration areas across your environment.

name: inventory__crownJewels
description:
Validates whether the specified resources are marked as  as crown jewels — high-value or business-critical assets.

If none of the provided resources are marked as crown jewels, the response will be empty.

Use this endpoint to programmatically verify the crown jewel status of specific resources across your environment.

name: inventory__resolveResourceType
description:
Takes a free-form resource-type string (e.g. "eks_cluster", "ec2 instance", "s3", "kubernetes pod") and returns the closest matching canonical resource type names supported by inventory.

Match order: (1) exact, (2) curated alias map for common LLM guesses, (3) substring on canonical name, (4) all-tokens-present fuzzy match.

Use this BEFORE calling inventory__list with a guessed resource_type to avoid the "Invalid resource type" error round-trip.

name: investigator__investigate
description:
Retrieves detailed investigative data for a specified resource within a given time range. This endpoint is intended for resource-focused investigations, providing activity and network context to assess potential compromise or misuse.

The response includes identity logs showing actions performed by principals (with source IP, identity details, destinations, error codes, and activity counts), process logs for commands executed on the resource (including parent binary, arguments, container, last seen time, and execution count), and flow logs describing network connections to other services, endpoints, or the internet (with traffic volume, destination details, and DNS names).

This endpoint is used to conduct in-depth investigations into a resource’s activity and connections.

name: investigator__summary
description:
Performs an AI-driven investigation of a resource’s activity within a specified time range and returns a concise summary. The analysis provides a verdict, confidence score, and contextual reasoning, highlighting whether the behavior appears benign, suspicious, or malicious, and why.

Use this endpoint to rapidly assess a resource’s activity through AI investigation.

name: investigator__triage

name: investigator__identityLogs

name: investigator__events

name: investigator__internetIngress

name: investigator__resourceFlowlogs

name: investigator__processLogs

name: network__trafficLogs
description:
Retrieves comprehensive network traffic logs from monitored environments, including connection metadata, source and destination details, protocol information, and traffic flow data.

Supports filtering by source/destination IP addresses, ports, protocols, connection states, traffic volumes, geographic regions, and time ranges.

Use this endpoint to analyze network communication patterns, identify suspicious traffic flows, and investigate connectivity issues across your infrastructure.

Paging is capped at 10,000 rows: `skip` + `limit` must not exceed it (400 otherwise) and `totalCount` saturates there — narrow the time range to reach older rows. Time bounds are RFC3339, e.g. "2026-08-18T09:00:00Z".

src_port_range.description: A number or a range of numbers (e.g. "5" or "5-10")

dst_port_range.description: A number or a range of numbers (e.g. "5" or "5-10")

from_timestamp.description: Start time (RFC3339, e.g. "2026-08-18T09:00:00Z"). REQUIRED — always provide both from_timestamp and to_timestamp

to_timestamp.description: End time (RFC3339, e.g. "2026-08-18T15:00:00Z"). REQUIRED — always provide both from_timestamp and to_timestamp

name: network__trafficGraph
description:
Returns network traffic aggregated by the requested dimension (account, region, cluster_id, namespace, resource_type, dns_names, ip, or default).

Used by the runtime-map graph view to fetch each drilldown level on demand.

Pass cursor:null to page all results in stable identity order, following nextCursor until null. Without cursor, returns legacy top-N traffic buckets. size is a per-page limit.

Time bounds are UTC calendar days (YYYY-MM-DD), not RFC3339 instants. A request must cover 1-7 inclusive days.

account_ids.description: Runtime-map account filter. Matches when either endpoint belongs to one of the selected accounts.

drilldown_resource_type.description: Runtime-map hierarchy scope for a resource-type group. Kept separate from directional user filters.

drilldown_scope.description: Resource-leaf hierarchy ownership. When present, directional location filters only constrain their respective endpoints.

intermediate_resource_id.description: Match flows where this resource appears as either source or destination. Forwarded to ms_paths as top-level resource_id.

drilldown_provider.description: Runtime-map provider drilldown. When set, the server returns per-account rows scoped to this provider (no initial-state rollup).

drilldown_account.description: Runtime-map account drilldown. When set, the server returns resource-type group rows + cluster placeholder rows + inter-group edges scoped to this account.

from_timestamp.description: REQUIRED: first UTC calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD). The runtime-map rollup does not store sub-day timestamps.

to_timestamp.description: REQUIRED: last UTC calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive. The range from from_timestamp must contain 1-7 days.

cursor.description: Pass null for the first complete-result page, then nextCursor until null. Omit for the legacy top-N view.

name: simulation__simulateEventImpact
description:
Simulate the security impact of a proposed cloud resource change BEFORE it is applied. Returns the new rule violations the change would introduce and a summary of connectivity/permissions paths that would be created, closed, or modified — grouped by (src_type, dst_type) — separately for the network and permissions topologies.

Input: { changes: [{ account_id, region, resource_type, action: "created"|"modified"|"deleted", before?: <translated record>, after?: <translated record> }] }
Output: { simulation_timestamp, event_id, new_violations, path_impact_summary: { network, permissions }, errors }

USE THIS TOOL WHEN:
- You are about to call responseActions__invoke for a destructive runbook and want to evaluate blast radius first.
- A user is asking "what would happen if I did X" against a cloud resource.
- You want to compare the security posture before vs after a hypothetical change.
- You identified a potential fix or remediation and want to evaluate it BEFORE recommending it — simulate the change, then reason about the outcome (new violations, path impact) in your finding, citing the simulation as evidence.

HOW TO BUILD THE EVENTCHANGERECORD FOR A RUNBOOK PREVIEW:
1. Identify the resource(s) the runbook will modify (read the runbook description — it names the resource type and action).
2. Fetch the current translated state via inventory__details / inventory__configuration. That JSON IS your "before".
3. Synthesize the "after" by deep-copying the before and applying the mutation the runbook script performs.

VERBATIM COPY RULE (CRITICAL — most simulation failures come from violating this):
- `before` MUST be the EXACT translated JSON the inventory tool returned to you, byte-for-byte. Do NOT rename keys. Do NOT change capitalization. Do NOT pluralize/depluralize. Do NOT add fields the inventory record did not have. Do NOT remove fields you think are irrelevant. Do NOT reorder arrays. Whatever attribute name the inventory record used for an array (e.g. "Entries" vs "acl_entry" vs "Statement") is the name you keep.
- **`resource_id` is required on BOTH `before` AND `after`** — copy it from the inventory record exactly. If you omit it the simulator silently classifies the change as a no-op (sub_events_count=0, new_violations=[], errors contains "Change missing resource_id") and returns event_id=null. Common mistake: copying only the AWS-native fields (NetworkAclId, InstanceId, BucketName, etc.) and dropping `resource_id` because it "looks redundant". It is NOT — the simulator keys on `resource_id`.
- `resource_type` MUST be the inventory `resource_type` value (e.g. "pod", "security_group", "network_acl") copied verbatim from inventory__details — NOT a Terraform/cloud-prefixed guess like "aws_eks_pod" or "aws_security_group". The simulator keys on the inventory schema name; a prefixed or unknown type fails with an opaque 500 ("'str' object has no attribute 'get'").
- `after` MUST equal `before` in EVERY field except the precise mutation the runbook performs. The diff between them should be exactly one append, one flip, or one set — nothing else. If you see additional differences when you compare them, you have drifted from the schema; re-copy `before` from the inventory output.
- The simulator parses against the modeler's schema; mismatched/renamed keys are rejected with cryptic errors. When errors come back, the fix is almost always "go re-read the inventory record and copy it more literally."
- SELF-CHECK before sending: confirm `before.resource_id === after.resource_id` and both are the bare AWS short ID (e.g. "acl-bf0adec3", "i-0abc...", "subnet-...") — NOT a full ARN. The inventory record used the bare id; you do too.
4. Pass action="modified" with both before and after. For "created" provide only after; for "deleted" provide only before.
5. If the runbook touches multiple resources (e.g. dedup-by-NACL across multiple subnets), construct one EventChangeRecord per UNIQUE underlying resource — duplicates are wasted work.

INTERPRETING THE RESULT:
- new_violations[] — rule violations the change would introduce. Each has rule_name, severity ("low" | "medium" | "high" | "critical"), rule_type. "critical" or "high" violations are usually a strong "do not proceed" signal. If you need to act on a specific violation (rules__ruleViolations, rules__createExclusion), resolve the rule_id by calling rules__list({phrase: rule_name}) — rule_id is omitted from this output to save tokens.
- path_impact_summary.network.{new,closed,modified} — connectivity paths the change adds, removes, or alters. "closed" paths are usually intended for blocking-style remediations. "new" paths are usually unintended for blocking actions and a strong signal to investigate.
- path_impact_summary.permissions.* — same buckets but for IAM principal→resource paths.
- errors[] — simulation-side errors (modeler / analyzer). If present and non-empty, your before/after almost certainly drifted from the inventory schema; re-fetch and copy verbatim.
- **NO-OP SIGNAL** — if the result has `event_id: null` AND `sub_events_count: 0` AND `errors` mentions "missing resource_id" or both `network` and `permissions` summaries are entirely empty, the simulator did NOT actually run — your before/after were classified as identical or unparseable. Do NOT proceed to invoke based on a no-op result. Re-fetch the inventory record, re-construct the EventChangeRecord with `resource_id` set on BOTH sides, and call again. The simulation gate will refuse invoke until a SUCCESSFUL sim (event_id !== null) has run.

Do NOT use the Terraform/cloud-prefixed form ("aws_security_group", "aws_eks_pod"): the simulator keys on the inventory schema name and a prefixed/unknown type fails with an opaque 500.

name: responseActions__getOptions
description:
Get available response actions (runbooks) for a specific resource. Call this FIRST before invoking any response action — it returns the list of runbook IDs, names, and (when present) the schema of caller-supplied parameters the runbook needs.

Input: { detectedResourceId: "<inventory resource_id>", includeCodeForRunbookId?: "<runbook id>" }
Output: array of { id, name, description, caller_params_schema? } where caller_params_schema (if present) maps param name → { description, value_type: "string"|"integer"|"boolean"|"string_enum", enum?, required }. Use the id with responseActions__invoke and supply matching caller_params for every required entry.

RESOURCE ID RULE (CRITICAL): pass the resource_id EXACTLY as the detection / inventory tools gave it to you. Do NOT construct, expand, or "complete" it into an ARN. For AWS that id is usually the short native id ("i-0abc...", "vol-0abc...", "my-bucket"); for Azure it is the "/subscriptions/..." path and for GCP the "projects/..." path. The server can recover some simple constructed ARNs, but not all of them, and an id you invented is never more correct than the one you were handed.

READING AN EMPTY OR SHORT RESULT — three different situations, do NOT conflate them:
1. `error` is present → the resource_id did not resolve in inventory. A bad id, nothing more. Re-read the id from the detection and call again. Say NOTHING about remediation coverage.
2. `_filtered_by_agent_scope` is present → runbooks DO exist for this resource, but your agent config is not allowed to run them. Report a permissions boundary and recommend the action for a human. Do NOT call this missing coverage.
3. `is_remediation_stack_installed: false` with NO `error` → the remediation stack really is not deployed on that cloud account. This one you SHOULD report plainly as a missing integration; the listed runbooks (if any) will carry a `disabled_reason` saying the same. Recommend deploying the stack.
A resource-tag or account guardrail does not appear here at all — it surfaces when you call responseActions__invoke and is refused with the reason.

The list is never truncated — it contains every runbook you are PERMITTED to run on this resource. It is not necessarily every runbook that exists for it: an agent-level allowlist may have filtered it, so an empty or short list does NOT prove nothing can be done. If no listed runbook fits, emit a finding recommending human action rather than concluding no remediation exists. Each runbook's SSM script is omitted from `code` to keep the result small; the description tells you what the runbook does. If you need the script itself (only useful for predicting a runbook's exact mutation, i.e. the simulation flow), call this tool again with includeCodeForRunbookId set to that runbook's id. NEVER guess, increment, or construct a runbook id — only use ids returned by this tool.

name: responseActions__invoke
description:
Execute a response action (runbook) on a resource. You MUST call responseActions__getOptions first to discover available runbooks AND their caller_params_schema (if any), then use that information here.

Input: { runbookId: "<from getOptions>", resourceId: "<inventory resource_id>", caller_params?: { <key>: "<string>" } }

Use the SAME resource_id you passed to responseActions__getOptions — exactly as the detection / inventory tools gave it to you, never an ARN you constructed yourself.

WORKFLOW:
1. responseActions__getOptions({ detectedResourceId }) → get available runbooks AND their caller_params_schema
2. Choose the appropriate runbook based on the action needed (isolate, quarantine, revoke, etc.)
3. If the chosen runbook has a caller_params_schema, extract each required value from the detection / inventory data you have already collected (raw event fields, resource attributes, etc.) and put them in caller_params as strings. Validate against value_type/enum yourself before sending — the server will reject mismatches.
4. responseActions__invoke({ runbookId, resourceId, caller_params? }) → execute it.

CALLER_PARAMS RULES:
- Only send keys declared in caller_params_schema; the server rejects unknown keys.
- All values must be strings on the wire. Numbers like ports → "22", booleans → "true"/"false".
- For string_enum, the value must match one of the allowed enum entries exactly.
- Omit optional params when you do not have a confident value rather than guessing.

SIMULATION GATE (active only when your task description mentions "simulation"):
If the gate is active, this tool will refuse the first invoke for any runbook target until you have called simulation__simulateEventImpact since the last invoke. The refusal returns a synthetic message telling you to simulate first; the runbook does NOT fire. Workflow when gated:
  a. Call responseActions__getOptions to identify the runbook and read its description. Scripts are omitted by default, so to see exactly what it will do call getOptions again with includeCodeForRunbookId=<that runbook id> and read the returned SSM YAML.
  b. Use inventory__details / inventory__configuration to fetch the current translated state of the resource(s) the runbook will modify (for the EKS NACL runbook, that means the network_acl associated with the cluster's subnets).
  c. Construct the EventChangeRecord(s) — the before is the current translated state; the after is the same record with the mutation the runbook would perform applied (e.g. append a new entry to NACL Entries with RuleNumber=next_unused, RuleAction=deny, CidrBlock=<the IP from caller_params>/32, Egress=false, Protocol="-1").
  d. Call simulation__simulateEventImpact({ changes: [...] }) and inspect the result.
  e. Decide: if new_violations or path_impact_summary changes are acceptable, call responseActions__invoke. If the blast radius is unacceptable, EMIT a finding documenting which violations or paths concerned you and DO NOT call invoke.
  f. After invoke fires, if you need to invoke another runbook, repeat the simulation step — each invoke must be preceded by a fresh simulation when the gate is active.

name: agentActions__getOptions
agentActions__invoke
description:
Execute a runtime agent action (kill process, block IP, isolate pod, etc.) on a resource. You MUST call agentActions__getOptions first to verify the action is available and the agent is connected.

Input: { actionType: "<from getOptions>", parameters: { <key>: <value> }, resourceId: "<resource ID>", targetNode?: "<node name>", targetClusterId?: "<cluster ID>", targetInstanceId?: "<instance ID>", detectionId?: "<detection ID>" }

WORKFLOW:
1. agentActions__getOptions({ resourceId }) → discover available actions + confirm agent connectivity
2. agentActions__invoke({ actionType, parameters, resourceId, ... }) → dispatch the action
3. agentActions__getHistory({ resourceId }) → poll to check action status (pending → dispatched → success/failure)

IMPORTANT: Actions are dispatched asynchronously to distributed agents. The invoke call returns immediately with status "pending". Use getHistory to confirm the action completed successfully before reporting it as done.

ACTION SELECTION PROTOCOL:
1. Classify the threat from the detection — what is actually happening and what would genuinely contain it.
2. Read each option's description: what it does, "Use when", and "Do NOT use for".
3. Invoke the single action whose "Use when" matches the threat and whose parameters you can fill from verified evidence.
4. NEVER target the protected resource's own identifiers (e.g. its own IP) — act on the malicious REMOTE peer, not the victim resource.
5. If no action fits, do NOT invoke a best-effort substitute; emit a finding stating that no runtime-agent action applies and recommend a response-action runbook or manual escalation.

name: agentActions__getHistory
description: Query the execution history of runtime agent actions, optionally filtered by resource, detection, or action type. Use this to poll for action completion after invoking.

name: agentActions__cancel
description: Cancel a pending agent action before it is dispatched to the agent. Only actions in "pending" status can be cancelled.

name: agentActions__execReadOnlyShell
description:
Run a strictly READ-ONLY shell command on a resource (VM host, K8s pod container, or ECS task) through the connected runtime agent — the "Host Shell" / "Container Shell" capability, restricted to investigation.

WHAT IS ALLOWED: only inspection commands (cat, ls, ps, ss, netstat, lsof, ip, grep, find, journalctl, systemctl status/show, etc.), optionally chained with a single pipe (`|`). The command is validated server-side BEFORE dispatch; any write/mutating command, shell chaining (`;`, `&&`, `||`, `&`), command/parameter substitution (`$(...)`, backticks, `${...}`), output redirection (`>`, `>>`), privilege escalation (sudo/su) or a non-allowlisted binary is REJECTED and nothing is dispatched. This tool can NEVER modify the host.

WORKFLOW:
1. Optionally call agentActions__getOptions({ resourceId }) to confirm a runtime agent is connected.
2. agentActions__execReadOnlyShell({ resourceId, command, containerName? }) → dispatches asynchronously, returns { id, status: "pending" }.
3. agentActions__getHistory({ resourceId }) → poll until the matching action reaches a terminal status; the command output is in the action result.

Notes: each command runs independently via /bin/sh with a ~30s timeout. For K8s pods / ECS tasks pass containerName to target a specific container; leave it empty for VM/host resources (runs on the host).

name: agentActions__reportResults
description: Called by the runtime agent to report execution results for previously dispatched response actions.

name: users__preferences__get
description: Returns the current user's email-notification preferences.

name: users__preferences__update
description: Updates the current user's email-notification preferences.

name: workloads__summary
description: Retrieves AI workload detection signals for a specific resource, including providers, models, usage types, and confidence levels.

name: scannerDiscovery__ingest
description: Accepts disk-side AI-workload and secret findings from the agentless cloud-volume-scanner, one call per scanned resource. AI workloads are forwarded to the AI Workload detector; secrets are forwarded to ms_standards and applied as TTL-bounded LL_Secret_* resource tags. Cloud-agnostic — resource_type distinguishes AWS/Azure/GCP.

name: workspaces__list
description: Get workspaces

name: cve__listCves
description:
Retrieves a list of detected vulnerabilities (CVEs) across monitored environments, with details such as severity, CVSS score, exploit and fix availability, affected packages, impacted resources, and remediation guidance.

Supports filtering by CVE ID, account, resource, resource type, package name, severity, exploit availability, fix availability, internet exposure, and region. Results can be sorted by CVE ID, severity, CVSS score, discovery time, or published date.

Use this endpoint to review and prioritize vulnerabilities for remediation based on severity, exploitability, and exposure context.

name: cve__listCvesPost
description:
Retrieves a list of CVEs from PostgreSQL with full filtering, sorting, and pagination support.

Supports complex nested filters including tags, score comparisons, and date ranges.

Use this endpoint when you need advanced filtering capabilities not available in GET /cve.

name: cve__exportCves
description:
Exports CVEs matching the provided filters to CSV format.

Returns the CSV content as a string along with a suggested filename.

Supports all the same filters as the listCves endpoint.

name: cve__exportCveResources
description:
Exports resources affected by CVEs matching the provided filters to CSV format.

Returns the CSV content as a string along with a suggested filename.

name: cve__exportCveImages
description:
Exports container images affected by CVEs matching the provided filters to CSV format.

Returns the CSV content as a string along with a suggested filename.

name: cve__listFacets
description:
Returns distinct values for a specified facet field to populate filter dropdowns.

Supports filtering by cve_id, packages, resource_id, resource_tag_key, and resource_tag_value.

Results can be filtered by an optional phrase for autocomplete functionality.

For resource_id, the search matches both resource_id and display_name but returns only resource_ids.

For resource_tag_value, optionally provide tag_key to filter values by a specific key.

name: cve__getCveTrends
description:
Retrieves CVE trends from the cve_daily_aggregations table.

Array filters accept comma-separated values (e.g., severity=CRITICAL,HIGH).

For complex filters, use the POST /cve/trends/query endpoint instead.

name: cve__getCveTrendsPost
description:
Retrieves CVE trends from the cve_daily_aggregations table.

Supports grouping by severity, CVE ID, or account.

Supports time periods: past_week, past_month, past_year.

Can filter by CVE characteristics and risk factors.

Returns daily aggregated counts for charting and analysis.

name: cve__getCveSeveritySummary
description:
Retrieves current CVE counts grouped by severity from live tables (cve_details joined with resource_vulnerabilities and inventory_*).

Aggregation is computed on the fly against the latest generation; pre-aggregated daily tables are intentionally not used because they lose resolution needed by the filters.

Supports the same filters as the CVE list endpoint.

Returns severity counts for CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW.

Designed for pie chart visualization.

name: cve__listCveResources
description:
Retrieves a list of resources affected by specified CVE(s) with filtering and pagination.

Array filters accept comma-separated values (e.g., cve_ids=CVE-2021-44228,CVE-2021-45046).

For complex filters like tags, use the POST /cve/resources/query endpoint instead.

EXPOSURE VERDICT: each result row carries `internet_exposed`, `exposure_risk` and `exposure_risk_description`. These are the authoritative answer for whether THIS CVE is reachable on THAT resource — they already account for the CVE attack vector, the network path and reachability. A public IP, public DNS name or permissive security group read from inventory__details / inventory__configuration describes the HOST, not the vulnerability, and never overrides them: a local-vector CVE (CVSS AV:L) on a host with a public IP is still not remotely exploitable. Report exposure from these fields, and where a raw config attribute seems to disagree, cite the fields and treat the attribute as context only.

name: cve__listCveResourcesPost
description:
Retrieves a list of resources affected by specified CVE(s) with filtering and pagination.

Supports complex nested filters including tags.

Returns resource details including exposure risk, internet exposure status, and associated container images.

name: cve__listCveResourcesGrouped
description:
Returns resource counts grouped by a specified attribute (account, resource type, cluster, namespace, or region).

Useful for displaying aggregated views of affected resources.

name: cve__listCveImages
description:
Retrieves a list of container images affected by specified CVE(s) with filtering and pagination.

Returns image details including affected resource count, internet exposure status, and associated clusters/namespaces.

Supports filtering by CVE IDs, image ID, account, resource type, region, cluster, and namespace.

name: cve__listCvesGrouped
description:
Returns CVEs grouped by a specified attribute (currently only packages).

Each group includes total CVE count, exploitable CVE count, and severity breakdown.

Useful for displaying aggregated views of vulnerabilities in the resource panel.

name: cve__listResourceFacets
description:
Returns distinct values for a specified facet field to populate filter dropdowns in the CVE Resources view.

Supports filtering by account_id, resource_type, region, resource_id, vpc, cluster_id, namespace_id, container_images, and ticket_id.

Results can be filtered by an optional phrase for autocomplete functionality.

For resource_id, the search matches both resource_id and display_name but returns only resource_ids.

name: cve__resourceTicketFacets
description:
Returns ticket keys for the "Ticket Id" filter dropdown in the CVE Resources view.

Ticket data is served by the events service, not the CVE Postgres facets.

Filtered by an optional phrase for autocomplete; scoped to a CVE via filters.cve_ids.

name: cve__listImageFacets
description:
Returns distinct values for a specified facet field to populate filter dropdowns in the CVE Images view.

Supports filtering by image_id, image_type, registry_id, repository_id, account_id, cluster_ids, namespace_ids, and ticket_id.

Results can be filtered by an optional phrase for autocomplete functionality.

name: cve__getAiSummary
description:
Retrieves an AI-generated analysis of a specific CVE, including attack vector details, exploitation path, and contextual insights into how the vulnerability can be leveraged. The summary explains potential impact, exploitation requirements, and conditions that may limit or enable an attack.

Use this endpoint to quickly understand the technical implications and exploitation feasibility of a vulnerability before prioritizing remediation.

name: cve__getCve
description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific CVE by its ID.

name: cve__streamScanRaw
description:
Accepts raw SBOM data from K8s agents for asynchronous vulnerability scanning.

If the SBOM hash exists in cache, returns cached results immediately.

Otherwise, queues the SBOM for processing by periodic Grype job.

name: cve__streamScanImages
description: Returns a list of recently scanned images with their status.

name: cve__streamScanSbomHashes
description: Checks if a given SBOM hash exists in the cache, indicating it has already been scanned.

name: cve__streamScanImageDigests
description: Given a comma-separated list of manifest digests, returns the subset already present in the scan cache, each with the SBOM hash it was scanned as, so the caller can skip pulling those images while still recording the association.

name: cve__exclusions__specific__query
description:
Lists per-resource, per-controller, and per-image vulnerability exclusions. Optionally filter by CVE id (cveId, integer form) or subject id (resource_id or image digest). Returns each exclusion with its id, CVE int id, subject kind (resource/image), subject id, who excluded it, the comment, and the exclusion timestamp.

IMPORTANT: cveId must be the integer ID from cve__listCves results, not the CVE string label.

name: cve__exclusions__specific__add
description:
Manage CVE exclusions. Two scopes:
1. Specific exclusion (cve__exclusions__specific__add): exclude individual resources, controllers (Deployments/ASGs — controlled resources auto-excluded), or container images from a single CVE.
2. Full CVE exclusion (cve__exclusions__cve__add): exclude an entire CVE customer-wide — all current and future affected resources are hidden.

WORKFLOW:
- Use cve__listCves to find the CVE and its integer id (numeric primary key, NOT the "CVE-2024-xxxx" label).
- For specific exclusions: use cve__listCveResources to find affected resource_ids/image digests, then call cve__exclusions__specific__add with subjects array.
- For full CVE exclusions: call cve__exclusions__cve__add with the integer cveId(s).
- Always provide a non-empty comment explaining the exclusion reason.
- To undo: query existing exclusions via the query endpoints, then call the corresponding delete endpoint with the exclusion UUIDs.

IMPORTANT: cveId must be the integer ID from cve__listCves results (the numeric primary key), NOT the CVE label string like "CVE-2024-1234". subjects[].kind is either "resource" (use resource_id / ARN — also works for controllers like Deployments, ASGs) or "image" (use image digest). A non-empty comment is REQUIRED — explain why this exclusion is being created.

name: cve__exclusions__specific__delete
description:
Removes one or more per-resource/per-controller/per-image exclusions by their exclusion ids (the id returned by the specific.query and specific.add endpoints). After deletion the underlying resources/images reappear in CVE views and the attack-path engine will reconsider them on the next modeler run. Returns the count of rows actually deleted.

IMPORTANT: exclusionIds are UUIDs returned by cve__exclusions__specific__query or cve__exclusions__specific__add, not CVE IDs.

name: cve__exclusions__specific__countByCveId
description: Returns a per-CVE count of how many specific (resource / controller / image) exclusions exist. Useful for surfacing exclusion badges next to each CVE in a list, or for deciding whether a CVE has been partly muted before deciding to entirely exclude it.

name: cve__exclusions__cve__query
description: Lists CVEs that have been excluded customer-wide. Each entry represents a CVE that is hidden across every view, every count, and the attack-path engine — including future affected resources. Returns exclusion id, CVE int id, CVE label (e.g. CVE-2025-1234), severity, who excluded it, the comment, and the exclusion timestamp.

name: cve__exclusions__cve__add
description:
Manage CVE exclusions. Two scopes:
1. Specific exclusion (cve__exclusions__specific__add): exclude individual resources, controllers (Deployments/ASGs — controlled resources auto-excluded), or container images from a single CVE.
2. Full CVE exclusion (cve__exclusions__cve__add): exclude an entire CVE customer-wide — all current and future affected resources are hidden.

WORKFLOW:
- Use cve__listCves to find the CVE and its integer id (numeric primary key, NOT the "CVE-2024-xxxx" label).
- For specific exclusions: use cve__listCveResources to find affected resource_ids/image digests, then call cve__exclusions__specific__add with subjects array.
- For full CVE exclusions: call cve__exclusions__cve__add with the integer cveId(s).
- Always provide a non-empty comment explaining the exclusion reason.
- To undo: query existing exclusions via the query endpoints, then call the corresponding delete endpoint with the exclusion UUIDs.

IMPORTANT: cveIds must be an array of integer IDs from cve__listCves results (numeric primary keys), NOT CVE label strings like "CVE-2024-1234". A non-empty comment is REQUIRED — explain why this exclusion is being created.

name: cve__exclusions__cve__delete
description:
Removes one or more customer-wide CVE exclusions by their exclusion ids (the id returned by cve.query / cve.add). After deletion the affected CVEs reappear in every view and the attack-path engine will reconsider them on the next modeler run. Returns the count of rows actually deleted.

IMPORTANT: exclusionIds are UUIDs returned by cve__exclusions__cve__query or cve__exclusions__cve__add, not CVE IDs.

name: sbom__listPackages
description:
Returns the package inventory extracted from SBOMs, one row per package identity (normalized PURL).

Counts are per live workload: installed, plus the runtime breakdown (executed / loaded / not measured). A workload is the controller where the resource has one, so a ReplicaSet counts once however many pods run it (DEV-22080); callers that read these as pod counts will see smaller numbers.

Runtime status is only known for packages carrying a CVE today; everything else reports as not measured rather than zero.

group_by_name changes what a page is: limit and skip then apply to package NAMES rather than rows, the response carries every version of each name in the page, and total_count is the number of names. Left unset the endpoint behaves as before.

search.description: Free-text over package name (pg_trgm). Max 200 characters.

name: sbom__listPackageResources
description: Drill-down for one package: every live workload it is installed on, with runtime status, file paths and last scan. A row is a controller where the resource has one, so a ReplicaSet appears once however many pods run it, with resource_count giving the number behind the row (DEV-22080). The unit is the pod controller ownerReference, which for a Deployment is its ReplicaSet, so a rollout shows the old and new ReplicaSets as two rows while both have pods. Callers that counted rows as resources before this change will see fewer.

name: sbom__listPackageVulnerabilities
description:
One row per CVE, not per (CVE, resource): a CVE affecting this package on 96 machines is one thing to fix, and resource_count carries the blast radius.

Ordered by severity then EPSS - severity alone leaves a wall of criticals in arbitrary order, and EPSS is the only field here that says which are actually being exploited.

Scoped to resources that carry this package, so an unrelated CVE on the same machine is not attributed to it.

name: sbom__exportPackages
description:
Exports the packages matching the supplied filters and sort, not the whole table - the file has to agree with the view it was taken from.

The four runtime counts are separate columns rather than the collapsed on-screen label, so the file is pivotable.

Large result sets stop at a row cap and set `truncated`; a truncated CSV is indistinguishable from a complete one, so callers must surface it.

search.description: Free-text over package name (pg_trgm). Max 200 characters.

name: compliance__entities
description:
Lists the compliance standards/frameworks (e.g. CIS, SOC 2, PCI-DSS, NIST, HIPAA) tracked for the customer.

Returns each standard with its id, name, type, version, and description. Use this first to discover the available standards and their ids before querying scores, categories, or controls.

Supports filtering by id or name, free-text search, sorting, and pagination.

name: compliance__entitiesScores
description:
Returns compliance posture scores — the percentage of passing rules — per standard, category, control, or account.

The `score` is 0–100 (higher = more compliant); `total_rules` and `total_violated_rules` give the underlying counts. `group_by` selects the aggregation level — one of compliance_ids, compliance_categories_ids, compliance_controls_ids, or accounts (defaults to compliance_ids = one row per standard).

Filter by compliance standard ids, category ids, control ids, or accounts to scope the result. Call compliance__entities first if you need the standard ids.

name: compliance__accountScores
description:
Returns the compliance posture score per cloud account for a SINGLE compliance standard, letting you compare which accounts are most/least compliant.

REQUIRED: `filters.compliance_ids` must contain exactly one compliance standard id (get it from compliance__entities). Calling this without exactly one id is rejected.

Each result has the account, its `score` (0–100), and `total_violated_rules`.

name: compliance__categories
description:
Lists the categories (groupings of controls) within compliance standards.

Returns each category with its id, name, and description. Filter by `compliance_id` to list the categories of a specific standard. Use the category ids to drill into compliance__controls or to scope a compliance__entitiesScores query.

name: compliance__controls
description:
Lists the individual controls (specific requirements) within a compliance category or standard.

Returns each control with its id, name, and description. Filter by `category_id` to list the controls of a specific category. Pair with compliance__entitiesScores to see how each control is scoring.

name: compliance__scoresChart
description:
Returns the compliance score over time as a time series, for trend analysis (is posture improving or degrading?).

Each point has a `period` and the `score` (0–100) at that time. Use `period` to set the granularity and filter by compliance standard/category/control ids or accounts to scope the trend.

name: aev__resolveTarget
description:
AEV scope gate. Confirms the resource is internet-facing per Stream, resolves the public host to probe (its own public address, or the fronting load balancer via associated resources), and mints a signed grant the plugin validates before probing.

Returns in_scope:false with a reason (and no grant) when the resource is not internet-facing or no public fronting host can be resolved — nothing downstream may probe it.

Always call this with the VULNERABLE resource’s own ID, never a fronting load balancer / API Gateway / CDN — this resolver discovers and probes through the fronting edge itself.

resource_id.description: ID of the VULNERABLE asset itself (the resource the internet_exposed finding names) — e.g. the EC2 instance, pod, or Lambda, never a fronting load balancer / API Gateway / CDN. This resolver auto-discovers the fronting edge from the attack-path graph and probes through it; passing the fronting edge’s own ID instead returns in_scope:false (it rarely carries the finding itself).

plugin_slug.description: Slug of the AEV plugin that will run the probe (its 24-hex plugin id is also accepted as a fallback). The grant is signed with that plugin’s key so only it can use the grant.

auth_contexts.description: Synthetic test identities for authenticated breach validation. Omit for unauthenticated probing. Do NOT pass a real production credential — these are for scoped test identities only.

label.description: Name the probe references this identity by (e.g. "user_a", "admin"). "anonymous" is reserved for sending no auth and needs no entry.

headers.description: Headers the probe attaches to the target request for this identity, e.g. {"Authorization":"Bearer …"} or a session {"Cookie":"…"}.

name: aev__mintOobToken
description: Mints + registers an out-of-band callback token and URL. The agent embeds the URL in a blind (HTTP) validation payload; a callback confirms the payload reached and ran on the in-scope target. callback_url is absent when no public host can be determined (degrade to detection-only).

callback_host.description: Public host the target should call back to. Optional — defaults to the request host.

name: aev__pollInteraction
description: Returns any callbacks recorded for the token. hit:true confirms a blind validation payload ran on the in-scope target (it issued the out-of-band callback). Tokens are scoped to the customer that minted them.
